terms.definition: One of the 600 tetrahedral cells of the 600-cell; each cell carries 433 sticker slots.
terms.ui: Local and Global views (cell outlines); cell names such as C013 in inspection and filters

terms.definition: A fixed place for one sticker; the full model has 600 x 433 = 259,800 slots. The mechanical state always keeps all of them; display filters may hide some from drawing, never from the state.
terms.ui: Views draw all slots unless a display filter hides some; inspection shows slot numbers

terms.definition: The identity of the sticker that sits in a slot; the state of the puzzle is the list of all 259,800 labels.
terms.ui: Inspection panel; exact-label progress; colour is drawn from the label

terms.definition: A rigid group of stickers that always moves together; a piece occupies one position and its stickers fill that position's slots.
terms.ui: Picking, inspection and tracking act on pieces

terms.definition: The set of pieces cut off around one cell pole that turns as one unit; a legal turn rotates exactly one cap.
terms.ui: Grip highlight in Local; the cap a key will turn

terms.definition: The choice of which cap the next twist turns; choosing a grip changes nothing in the puzzle state.
terms.ui: Grip keys of the keyboard; grip marker in Local

terms.definition: A turn of the gripped cap in one legal direction; every twist is one of the 1,200 generators or its inverse.
terms.ui: Twist keys; the move list and history

terms.definition: One of the 1,200 legal basic turns, numbered 1 to 1200; a negative number is its inverse. Every operation expands into generators.
terms.ui: Move counts, macro text, history

terms.definition: A class of positions whose pieces legal moves can exchange; the 35 moving orbits are numbered O0 to O34, pieces never leave their orbit, and the 600 fixed cell-centre pieces never move and are not numbered.
terms.ui: Orbit selector; per-orbit progress and residuals; filters such as O33

terms.definition: A legal word, one per orbit, whose effect on that orbit is a cycle of three pieces.
terms.ui: Macro base (per orbit); star construction details

terms.definition: What a word moves outside the orbit being worked on; 23 of the 35 raw seeds have collateral, and it is always kept, never discarded.
terms.ui: Complete-effect panel; support and conflict lists before execution

terms.definition: The order of orbits in which every seed's collateral falls on orbits not yet solved, so that finished orbits stay solved at every macro boundary.
terms.ui: Orbit list order; next-orbit suggestions
terms.source: solving-workflow.md section 2; technical report, 'Triangular stage invariant'

terms.definition: The solver's instruction that an orbit, position, piece or block must not change; an operation that would change it is refused, not hidden.
terms.ui: Protection indicator on every view; conflict warnings in preview
terms.source: session.py Session.preview and commit (protected orbits); solving-workflow.md section 3.3

terms.definition: Net checks protection on the complete operation's end result; Strict checks after every generator. An unchecked part is shown as unchecked, never as safe.
terms.ui: Protection check mode in preview

terms.definition: One of two fixed positions, A and B, chosen for an orbit; pieces pass through them while others are placed. A buffer is a place, not a piece.
terms.ui: A and B markers in Local; buffer keys

terms.definition: The piece currently sitting in a position; a buffer's occupant changes every time a star runs.
terms.ui: Inspection; buffer status line

terms.definition: The position X the solver wants to fill next; the solver always names it, the program never chooses it alone.
terms.ui: Target marker; candidate list with reasons

terms.definition: A word S, chosen for a target, that carries the reference position to the target X without moving the buffers; a star runs S^-1 first and S last.
terms.ui: Prepare phase of the work sheet; proposed setups for a named target

terms.definition: The fixed word that moves the seed's three-cycle onto buffer A, buffer B and a reference position.
terms.ui: Star construction details

terms.definition: The macro that cycles buffer A to B to target X; in chronological order it runs setup^-1, relocation^-1, the seed, relocation, setup (as Model.expand writes it). Its inverse cycles A to X to B.
terms.ui: Macro base (star macros); preview of the cycle
terms.source: solving-workflow.md section 3.1; core.py Model.star_net and expand

terms.definition: The position where a piece belongs when the puzzle is solved.
terms.ui: Home and current structure toggle; home(C...) filters
terms.source: core.py Filters (home and current predicates); solving-workflow.md section 3.3

terms.definition: A group of pieces the solver declares as an achievement, with members, required positions or relations, a reference and a preservation policy; Home blocks and referenced blocks are distinct.
terms.ui: Block panel; block boundary in Local; block protection

terms.definition: An ordered choice of reference stickers that fixes how a piece or block is oriented; a transported frame is the same frame carried along by moves.
terms.ui: Reference and frame display in Local; frame comparison of hidden buffers

terms.definition: Everything an operation does to all 259,800 labels, including regions hidden by filters; checks and protection always use it.
terms.ui: Preview: cycles, collateral, support, conflicts

terms.definition: A saved operation with its roles and three phases, Prepare, Macro and Cleanup; reusing it always triggers a fresh review.
terms.ui: Work sheet editor; phase editor

terms.definition: How a piece sits in its position; a piece can be at Home but wrongly oriented.
terms.ui: Orientation marks in Local; orientation_wrong counts

terms.definition: The group of ways a piece of an orbit can be turned in place: trivial, C2, C5, D5 or A5; it limits what can remain in the last buffer.
terms.ui: Orbit details; endgame stage display

terms.definition: The operation P_X(q) = K_{X,q} K_X^-1, built from stars: on the working orbit it fixes every position and moves an orientation change from X to a buffer; like every star product, it may also move pieces of other orbits (collateral), which preview shows.
terms.ui: Endgame tools; both ends shown in preview

terms.definition: What is still wrong in an orbit: pieces not at Home, wrong buffer occupants, wrong orientations and unknown frames; the final buffer may keep only a residual the orientation group allows.
terms.ui: Residuals panel per orbit; stage display; completion

terms.definition: A raw seed followed by corrections of all its collateral through previously built pure controllers; its net effect touches only its own orbit.
terms.ui: Macro base (advanced); theory book
